why: Quote is verbatim (page line 35; whole line read, nothing in it reverses the claim), and every code fact in ourState checks out: apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:2 says 'the read-only configuration checkup'; :21-23 say 'never repairs anything'; apps/cli/src/index.ts:2149 registers `doctor` as a CLI subcommand dispatched above the server-URL requirement; packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:20-33 carries the '## Scope, and what is deliberately outside it' block; `grep -ra -F checkup` finds no command registration and apps/electron/resources/skills holds only plugin-creator and skill-creator, so there is no /doctor or /checkup slash surface. What refutes the finding is its load-bearing framing: 'The narrowed scope is a recorded decision in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md (status: closed), which predates this tier change.' That is inverted. The w28 page header reads 'Week 28 · July 6-10, 2026', 'Releases v2.1.202 -> v2.1.206', and the /doctor feature pill is 'v2.1.205'. The plan is dated 2026-07-29 -- three weeks AFTER -- and at line 78 it quotes the exact tier change: 'Before v2.1.205, `/doctor` was a built-in command rather than a bundled skill.' Its section '4. What was deliberately left out' then enumerates precisely the w28 items: 'The interactive `/doctor` slash surface -- deviation 1 below. It is the half that "proposes fixes it applies only after you confirm" (:44), which is a different product from a read-only report'; 'Installation health, unused extensions, duplicate subagent names, and the checked-in-`CLAUDE.md` trim check ... Named here so the gap is a decision rather than an oversight'; and 'A `--fix` / repair mode.' It is filed as Deviation 1 with a category string and a cost ('1 small slice'), and scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py has already harvested it into docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md under '### plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md'. So it is a recorded, reasoned, register-tracked deviation authored with full knowledge of the v2.1.205 change, not an unrecorded divergence. (It is not one of the nine docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 owner decisions -- those are inert identifiers -- but it is the same class: a decision with a reason.) One layer down, the consequence is also weaker than stated: the fork already has the tier the doc needs -- ensureBundledSkills (packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:92) plus SessionManager.skillSlashCommands surface every bundled skill as /<slug> -- so the remainder is one resources/skills/doctor/SKILL.md plus a diagnostics seam on SessionToolContext (session-tools-core cannot import server-core), which is exactly what the plan costs out, not an architectural gap. Per the repo's rule that a plan is where a deviation's reason lives, this is refuted as a re-report of a closed decision.
correctedState: The code facts are right but the framing is wrong. `doctor` is intentionally a read-only CLI subcommand (`nessy-general-agent doctor`) with no fix flow, no confirmation step and no `/checkup` alias, and that narrowing is recorded Deviation 1 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md (status: closed, dated 2026-07-29) -- which POSTDATES the w28 tier change (Week 28 = July 6-10, 2026; /doctor pill v2.1.205) by three weeks and explicitly cites it via slash-commands.md:30 ('Before v2.1.205, `/doctor` was a built-in command rather than a bundled skill'). The plan names the interactive slash surface, the unused-extension / duplicate-subagent / CLAUDE.md-trim checks and a `--fix` repair mode as deliberately out of scope, with reasons: settings.md:311-312 requires `claude doctor` to keep working when the version gate refuses to start the app, so the terminal form is the load-bearing surface. The deviation is in the generated register under `### plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md`. The bundled-skill tier already exists (ensureBundledSkills + skillSlashCommands, seeding only plugin-creator and skill-creator today); closing the remainder is one resources/skills/doctor/SKILL.md plus a managed-diagnostics seam on SessionToolContext, already costed at '1 small slice'.
